# Training Setup and Baselines
## Overview
This family defines reference training protocols for [differentiable volume rendering](#43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md), establishing hyperparameters, optimization strategies, and architectural configurations for radiance field models [G]. It differs from its siblings by covering diverse representations including HDR tone-mapped [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) [11349-nerf-gt-baseline-training-setup.md], GAN-based radiance fields [12972-stylegan2-training-configuration.md], feature-volume NeRF [13271-nerf-training-setup.md], and light-field baselines [15254-nlr-baseline.md] [G].
## Shared principles
All children build on the core [differentiable volume rendering pipeline](#5583-differentiable-volume-rendering-pipeline.md) defined in [NeRF Training Loop](1522-training-loop-setup.md) [G].
## Subtopics

### [NeRF-GT Baseline Training Setup](11349-nerf-gt-baseline-training-setup.md)
Establishes a reference protocol for NeRF using HDR inputs, serving as an upper-bound for methods synthesizing HDR from LDR. It differs from [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) by explicitly handling dynamic range mismatch via tone-mapping during loss computation. Choose this when evaluating HDR reconstruction capabilities. [G]

### [StyleGAN2 Training Configuration](12972-stylegan2-training-configuration.md)
Defines the [training protocol](#4528-training-protocol.md) for StyleGAN2-based radiance fields (e.g., StyleNeRF, VoxGRAF). It solves [GAN](#14030-adversarial-training-gan.md) instability in 3D by enforcing R1 regularization, specific learning rate scaling, and removing 2D noise injection to preserve 3D consistency. Choose this for generative 3D-aware models. [G]

### [NeRF Training Setup](13271-nerf-training-setup.md)
Describes the configuration for NeRF-based models using Nerfstudio/Instant-NGP, focusing on fast convergence for static scenes. It details [Control-NeRF](#13260-control-nerf.md)'s use of [feature volumes](#18218-voxel-and-grid-representations.md) instead of raw coordinates for the fine network. Choose this for efficient static scene reconstruction. [G]

### [NLR Baseline](15254-nlr-baseline.md)
Implements the Neural Lumigraph Representation (NLR) as a foundational reference for differentiable volume rendering. It differs from standard NeRF by using an architecture optimized for light fields rather than a static MLP. Choose this for meta-learning or light field baselines. [G]

### NeuralVDB Hyperparameter Configuration
Configures training for [sparse volume representations](#5-sparse-structures.md) using hierarchical neural networks [S1, unofficial]. It addresses the trade-off between noise reduction and computational efficiency in VDB-based rendering [S1, unofficial]. Choose this when high-resolution sparse volume reconstruction is required [S1, unofficial].
*   **Step:** Batch sampling strategy is either drawing $2^{16}$ random samples per epoch, or resampling a subset of input voxels at fixed intervals (100 or 500) and drawing $2^{12}$ batches per epoch. The resampled subset size equals the resampling intervals multiplied by the batch size. Resampling is used when fine details with thin structures are critical [S1, unofficial].
*   **Parameter:** Subdomain size must be a multiple of 512. Too large wastes compute on empty subdomains; too small increases dispatch overhead and causes dominant overlapping halo regions leading to redundant computation [S1, unofficial]. Network width: Level-1 networks use half the width of level-0 networks. Default starting point: level-0 width 128, depth 3. Use 4 layers for volumes requiring more detail capture [S1, unofficial]. Optimizer: Adam with default learning rate 0.001. Decay: 0.975 every 100 epochs (no resampling) or 0.75 every 1,000 epochs (with resampling). Max epochs: 2,500 for non-resampled; more for resampled cases [S1, unofficial].
*   **Comparison:** Dense grid training produces the highest noise. Block grid (dense leaf nodes without active masks) reduces noise but still shows visible fog artifacts. Sparse [VDB](#1508-openvdb-vdb.md) with active [voxel masks](#1281-voxel-occupancy-test.md) yields the best visual quality and low noise reconstruction [S1, unofficial].

### Neural Codebook Training Configuration
Configures training for compact real-time radiance fields using a [Neural Codebook](#11912-neural-codebook.md) (NCB) [S2]. It focuses on efficient storage and fast inference through [codebook quantization](#23296-codebook-quantization.md) [G]. Choose this for real-time applications requiring [compact representation](#1349-ssvdag-node-layout-and-tagged-pointer-encoding.md) [G].
*   **Step:** Multiply learning rate by 0.3 for every 5,000 iterations. Cast the trained Neural Codebook (NCB) to float16 after training [S2].
*   **Parameter:** Optimizer: Adam with $\beta_1 = 0.9$ and $\beta_2 = 0.999$. Weight decay: $1e-5$. Initial learning rate: $5e-3$. Total training iterations: 20,000. Batch size: 100,000 voxels [S2].
